Vendor Profile

Black Duck by Synopsys

Open-source security, licence compliance, and static code analysis – helping software-building organisations find and fix vulnerabilities before they reach production.

Security DevOps

Overview

Black Duck by Synopsys provides application security testing tools that identify security vulnerabilities, open-source licence risks, and code quality issues in software during development – before applications are deployed. The core Black Duck product is a Software Composition Analysis (SCA) tool: it scans a codebase or build artifact to identify every open-source component included, checks each component against known CVE databases, and flags any licence obligations that may conflict with the organisation's commercial or regulatory requirements. The Coverity product adds static application security testing (SAST), analysing source code for security defects and coding errors that could introduce vulnerabilities.

Black Duck is used by organisations that build software internally – whether that is a financial services firm developing trading systems, a defence contractor writing embedded firmware, or an engineering company writing control software for physical products. Any organisation that includes open-source libraries in its software (which is nearly all of them) has an obligation to understand what vulnerabilities those libraries carry. Black Duck automates that process at the scale a modern development pipeline requires.

Arrow ECS UK's Black Duck book is small in transaction count (20 lines in 2025) but high in deal value – individual deals reaching £450,000 for large enterprise licence transactions. The end-user profile confirmed in Arrow's sales data spans financial services, engineering and manufacturing, professional services, and technology companies. Arrow sells both on-premises (Team model) and cloud-hosted (SaaS) deployment models.

Static Application Security Testing that analyses source code for security vulnerabilities, coding errors, and defects. Available on-premises (team licence, per developer) and as a SaaS offering via Polaris. Confirmed in Arrow 2025 sales data in both forms.

Cross-sell & Expansion Opportunities

IBM
DevSecOps – Black Duck in the IBM Software Pipeline
Customers using IBM DevOps tools (IBM UrbanCode Deploy, IBM Engineering Lifecycle Management) are building CI/CD pipelines where Black Duck can be integrated as a scanning stage. Black Duck supports API-based integration with Jenkins, GitHub Actions, and other pipeline tools commonly used alongside IBM DevOps platforms. IBM UK itself appears as an end user of Black Duck through Arrow's 2025 sales channel – confirming co-deployment at enterprise scale. Any IBM DevOps conversation in a software-building organisation should include a discussion of open-source security posture.
F5 Networks
Secure the Code, Protect the App at Runtime
Black Duck finds vulnerabilities in application code and dependencies during development. F5's Web Application Firewall protects the deployed application from exploitation at runtime. The two operate at different stages of the application security lifecycle and address different threat vectors – Black Duck reduces the attack surface before deployment; F5 mitigates the risk from what reaches production. Organisations with F5 WAF deployments that also have internal development teams are a natural Black Duck expansion conversation.
Entrust
Scan Before You Sign – SBOM + Code Signing
A complete software release chain for regulated organisations includes both scanning (confirming the code is clean) and signing (proving the release is authentic and untampered). Black Duck handles the scan; Entrust nShield HSMs provide the hardware-protected signing keys. In any organisation running a formal software release process – particularly in defence, financial services, or government supply chains – the combination addresses two mandatory security controls that are often bought separately without the connection being made.
OPSWAT
Supply Chain Security + OT Environment Protection
Black Duck ensures the software being deployed into an environment is free from known open-source vulnerabilities. OPSWAT controls what files and media can enter the operational environment where that software runs – particularly in air-gapped or OT environments. The two sit at different points in the same security chain: Black Duck verifies software provenance; OPSWAT controls physical data ingress. Particularly relevant for industrial and defence customers deploying software updates into isolated environments.

Competitive Landscape

The application security testing market is active. The primary alternatives to Black Duck in SCA and SAST are well established.

SNYK
SCA / Developer Security
SNYK is the most commonly encountered Black Duck alternative in SCA. SNYK leads on developer experience – it is designed to be used directly by developers in the IDE and CLI, whereas Black Duck is often deployed as a pipeline gate by security teams. Black Duck has advantages in licence compliance depth and binary scanning capability. Both are also Arrow vendors – position as complementary where possible; understand which motion the customer is already invested in. Note: SNYK is also listed in the IBM cross-sell context.
Checkmarx
SAST / SCA
Checkmarx competes with Coverity in SAST and has added SCA capability. Checkmarx One is its unified platform. Often encountered in mid-market accounts where a simpler unified toolset is preferred over Black Duck's more configurable approach. Coverity is generally considered deeper for complex enterprise codebases and C/C++ heavy environments (where Coverity has the longest track record).
Veracode
SAST / SCA / DAST
Veracode is a cloud-native application security testing platform covering SAST, SCA, and DAST. Well-established in financial services and regulated industries. Competes with both Coverity (SAST) and Black Duck (SCA). Veracode's strength is its all-in-one SaaS model; Black Duck's is depth of SCA capability and on-premises deployment for air-gapped environments.
GitHub Advanced Security
SCA / SAST (native tooling)
GitHub Advanced Security includes CodeQL (SAST) and Dependabot (SCA) as native GitHub features. Available to organisations already on GitHub Enterprise. Often used as a baseline or supplementary tool; lacks the depth of commercial SCA for complex dependency graphs, licence compliance, or binary analysis. Black Duck typically wins when compliance and audit requirements demand dedicated tooling rather than CI/CD-native scanning.

Ideal Customer Profile

Organisation Size
Mid-market to large enterprise. Black Duck's Team model pricing scales with developer count – it is cost-effective for organisations with 20+ developers and becomes increasingly attractive at larger scale. Arrow's book confirms enterprise-level deal sizes.
Verticals
Any organisation that builds software internally. Financial services, defence and aerospace, engineering and manufacturing, professional services, and technology companies. Arrow's 2025 sales data confirms end users in financial services, precision engineering, and technology sectors.
Trigger Events
SBOM requirement (NIS2, US EO 14028, UK NCSC guidance); open-source licence audit finding; supply chain security programme; DevSecOps maturity initiative; M&A due diligence on acquired software; CVE incident in open-source dependency.
Key Personas
Application Security Lead, DevOps / DevSecOps Manager, Head of Software Engineering, CISO (for policy mandate). Black Duck decisions often involve both the security team (who mandate it) and the engineering team (who use it).
